title: Fleet Orchestrator: Scale Manifest and Change Ledger UI
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Add a composable Scale Manifest editor and a Change Ledger (immutable change history) to the Fleet Orchestrator UI. This work scopes three coordinated console surfaces: the scaling controls (manifest authoring + presets), the throughput dashboard (live + historical token throughput and effective headroom), and the change ledger (audit trail with diffs and rollback affordances).

Goals:
- Enable operators to declare desired fleet capacity and autoscaling policy in a single manifest that is validated before apply.
- Surface effective throughput, percent headroom, and autoscale triggers so PMs and SREs can reason about guarantees vs observed behavior.
- Preserve a tamper-proof chronological ledger of all scaling changes (who, when, what), including human edits, API-driven updates, and automated rollouts, with clear rollback links to revert a manifest version.

Out of scope: low-level runtime autoscaler algorithm changes (handled in ENG), per-instance debug logs, and dedicated-pool provisioning flows that remain in the capacity backend APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Scale Manifest editor: create/update YAML manifest with schema validation and live preview of interpreted capacity (dedicated GPU pools, min/max replicas, burst windows, weightings)
Presets: read/write presets (operator-owned) and ability to apply preset to fleet with single-click preview of delta
Throughput Dashboard: 1m/5m/1h charts for tokens/sec, request rate, and utilization; ability to overlay manifest time ranges and annotations
Change Ledger: immutable entries for each manifest apply with user, timestamp, diff view, links to PR/issue, and a rollback action that re-applies a previous manifest version
Policy simulation: simulate applying a manifest against historical telemetry and show projected under/over provision windows
RBAC: only users with fleet-admin role can apply manifests or rollback; viewers can comment and propose changes
comments: 2025-01-23 — Initial scoping review with Eng (Nina Patel) and Design (Marco Ruiz). Eng flagged need for an API change to return interpreted capacity per-fleet; spike added to ENG-4822.

2025-01-28 — Design review: provided low-fidelity mockups (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/fleet-scale-mockups) showing inline validation and diff preview. Design requested an "impact ribbon" showing estimated cost delta.
2025-01-30 — PM sync: proposed rolling apply vs immediate apply flow. Consensus to default to "Rollout with Canary" for first release; follow-up ticket for immediate apply UX.

2025-02-03 — Security review notes: ensure ledger entries include an immutable manifest checksum and that rollback updates are logged as new ledger entries. Security approval required before shipping (TBD).

2025-02-05 — Linked artifacts: PRD (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DC/Fleet+Orchestrator+Scale+Manifest), API spec draft (https://gist.github.com/lia-m/scale-manifest-spec), and a GitHub draft PR for console components (https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1724).

2025-02-06 — Decision: MVP will not include CSV export (deferred) but will include an API endpoint to stream ledger entries for compliance export. Follow-up: PM-53199 to add CSV export and scheduled reporting.
next_steps: Finalize manifest schema with Eng (owner: Nina Patel) — target 2025-02-12
Design hi-fi and accessible components for diff/ledger views (owner: Marco Ruiz) — target 2025-02-14
Eng implement read-only interpret API (ENG-4822) and ledger write hook into audit-log service — target 2025-02-20
Wire up RBAC checks and enable canary rollout default in console (owner: Liam O'Connor) — target 2025-02-25
notes: Trade-offs discussed: exposing full YAML for power users vs a form-based editor. We will ship both: a form-first editor with a "raw YAML" toggle to reduce risk of malformed manifests.
Monitoring: tie throughput dashboard to existing telemetry (dataplane counters) and derive headroom as (manifest.max_capacity - observed_peak) / manifest.max_capacity.
Rollback semantics: rollback creates a new manifest identical to the selected historical version and records an explicit rollback reason; it does not delete ledger history.
